record.original_question: Is aabaacbaab 3-D0L-avoidable (i.e. is there a ternary morphism g such that g^^ω(a) avoids aabaacbaab)?

evidence.quote: Is aabaacbaab 3-D0L-avoidable (i.e. is there a ternary morphism g such that g^^ω(a) avoids aabaacbaab)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet. A morphism $g:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ is called prolongable on a letter $a\in\Sigma$ if $g(a)$ starts with $a$ and $|g^n(a)|\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$; in this case the iterated images $g^n(a)$ converge to a unique infinite word $g^\omega(a)\in\Sigma^\omega$, called the pure morphic (D0L) word generated by $g$ from $a$.

A pattern is a nonempty word $p$ over an alphabet of variables. An infinite word $w$ over $\Sigma$ is said to avoid $p$ if there is no nonerasing morphism $h$ from the variable alphabet to $\Sigma^+$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$. We say $p$ is $k$-D0L-avoidable if there exists an alphabet $\Sigma$ with $|\Sigma|=k$, a morphism $g:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ prolongable on some letter $a\in\Sigma$, such that the infinite word $g^\omega(a)$ avoids $p$.

Question. Take the pattern $p = aabaacbaab$ over the three variables $\{a,b,c\}$. Does there exist a morphism $g:\{0,1,2\}^*\to\{0,1,2\}^*$ prolongable on some letter $\alpha\in\{0,1,2\}$ such that the infinite word $g^\omega(\alpha)$ contains no factor of the form $h(aabaacbaab)$ for any nonerasing morphism $h:\{a,b,c\}^+\to\{0,1,2\}^+$? Equivalently, is the pattern $aabaacbaab$ 3-D0L-avoidable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of D0L-avoidability of the pattern aabaacbaab over a ternary alphabet appears in problem lists on pattern avoidance and ternary formulas (e.g., Ochem's notes on interesting ternary formulas). No source found in the search confirms a resolution; the problem appears to remain open, but no definitive recent reference proving or disproving it was located.

status_evidence.claim: The pattern is listed in a compilation of open ternary-avoidability questions; no resolution is indicated.
